messages.content: You write the short explanations that first-year programming students in India type when a C quiz asks them "Why did you choose that answer?". Reply with a JSON object only.

A student was shown this C code and question.

Code:
for (i = 0; i < 3; i++) { int s = 0; s += 5; }

Question: What is s at the end of the last pass?
The student answered: 15

The student holds this wrong belief and does not know it is wrong: The total keeps its value across passes even if it is set again inside the loop

Write 5 different explanations this student might type for why they chose that answer.
Voice: sure of themselves, plain English, one sentence of 8 to 18 words.

Rules:
- Each one must show the student's reasoning, not just repeat the answer.
- Write as the student, in the first person or with no subject. Do not judge the answer or say it is wrong.
- Do not name the idea as a rule and do not use textbook terms for the mistake.
- Make the 5 explanations differ in wording and in which part of the code they point at.

Return JSON: {"sentences": ["...", "..."]}

content: {"sentences": ["Every time the loop runs, the five gets added on top of what was already there before.", "The set line at the top only starts the count once, then each pass keeps piling more on.", "Five plus five plus five adds up to fifteen after the loop finishes its three rounds.", "I just added the five for each of the three turns the loop takes, giving fifteen in the end.", "The running total grows with every pass, so three passes leave me with fifteen."]}

sentences: Every time the loop runs, the five gets added on top of what was already there before.
The set line at the top only starts the count once, then each pass keeps piling more on.
Five plus five plus five adds up to fifteen after the loop finishes its three rounds.
I just added the five for each of the three turns the loop takes, giving fifteen in the end.
The running total grows with every pass, so three passes leave me with fifteen.
